speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To help me determine the cause, how would you describe the nature of this pain, and did it start after any specific injury or trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; pain severe enough to wake you from sleep and lack of relief with ibuprofen suggests an inflammatory or structural issue rather than simple osteoarthritis. Given your age and the chronic nature of the symptoms, have you noticed any stiffness when first getting out of bed in the morning, or does the pain worsen with activity and improve with rest?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) - Oligoarticular type. The clinical picture of a 24-year-old male (likely undiagnosed adult-onset JIA or seronegative spondyloarthropathy) with chronic night pain, swelling, morning stiffness, and lack of response to NSAIDs is highly suggestive of inflammatory arthritis. While septic arthritis and malignancy are rare in this chronic timeframe without trauma, the severity warrants immediate imaging and inflammatory markers. I will proceed with requesting blood work and imaging to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, ANA, HLA-B27. REQUEST IMAGES: Left Knee X-Ray, Left Knee MRI.
